Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

Untested theorycraft; no source publishes this build. It takes the Lord of Hatred skill-tree rework's headline new Sorcerer axis - Charged Bolts can be converted into a Fire skill - and asks whether that conversion is enough to carry the class's whole Fire scaling package on a projectile that moves instead of on a Firewall that does not. The class's meta build is the strongest single-target damage in the game by Maxroll's own week-1 read and is unplayably static by the same guide's admission: 'the moment you leave the Ring of Fire you suddenly deal no damage'. Everything the Fire package gives that build - the Fundamental Release buff from 10% to 30% per stack up to 90%, Habacalva's Cauldron's gentler Heat decay and non-expiring Overheat, Enchantment Master's Fire bonus from any orange enchantment - is attached to being a Fire Sorcerer, not to standing in a ring. The hypothesis is that a converted Charged Bolts build keeps all of it and pays only in single-target damage. It might not: Firewall's ceiling is an order of magnitude, and one order of magnitude is a lot of headroom to give away for mobility.

Rotation
  1. Hold Charged Bolts, drop Firewall on cooldown for the Burning, Teleport through packs rather than around them, and save Unstable Currents for a pack that deserves it.
  2. Ice Armor up throughout.
Variants

Leveling — Charged Bolts into the pack, Firewall under anything that survives, Teleport through rather than around. Watch one thing at this stage: does the Heat bar behave the way it does on a Firewall character? If Charged Bolts is not generating Heat, the conversion is not doing what this build needs and you have your answer in the first hour.
Move on when Level 70, Torment 1, and you have confirmed at a dummy that converted Charged Bolts counts as Fire. Do not progress this build on the assumption.

Early Endgame — Charged Bolts held down, Firewall dropped on cooldown for the Burning, Teleport to reposition, Unstable Currents on a pack that deserves it. Measure Overheat uptime here; it is the second of the two questions this build exists to answer.
Move on when Overheat measurably staying up while you move. If it does not, this build is a worse Firewall build and sorcerer-meta-firewall is the honest recommendation.

Late Endgame — Unchanged. This is the stage where the comparison against sorcerer-meta-firewall has to be run properly, on the same character's gear where possible, on both a pack and a lair boss.
Move on when The comparison is done and this build won something. If it won nothing, say so and go back.

Pushing — Untested at push tiers by definition, and the predicted result is a clear loss to sorcerer-meta-firewall on any floor whose damage check is a boss. The interesting question is not whether this out-pushes Firewall - it will not - but whether it clears the same floor in less real time. That is the number to bring back.

Uniques
  • helm Sorcerer class unique. Dedicated table: Grigoire, The Galvanic Saint, Hall of the Penitent south of Ked Bardu, Dry Steppes; 1x Lair Key from Helltide. Carried here for the Fire package rather than for Firewall specifically - which is itself part of what this build is testing. Where →
  • chest Sorcerer class unique. Dedicated table: Bartuc, via Infernal Hordes in Kehjistan near the Yshari Sanctum waypoint; 1x Infernal Hordes Compass, gather 666 Burning Aether. Where →
  • pants All-class unique from the General Unique Pool - any lair boss - and gamble pants at the vendor in parallel. Where →

Provenance, stated plainly: this allocation is the game-specialist's, not a published one. No source publishes a skill tree for this build because no source publishes this build - it is an untested hypothesis. The skills and their names come from knowledge/classes/sorcerer.md, which is the class-fact authority for the live season, and the point counts are a starting shape to test rather than a measured allocation. Every skill here ranks to 15 in the usual way.

Skill point priority

  1. Charged Bolts first, and take the Fire conversion the moment the tree offers it - without it this is just a worse Shock build
  2. Firewall kept on the bar through levelling because it is the cheapest Burning application while your gear is bad
  3. Teleport for mobility, which is the whole point
  4. Ice Armor for the barrier
  5. Hydra and Inferno as Fire filler

Board & glyph focus

Fundamental Release attaches early and deliberately - the 3.1.0 buff from 10% to 30% per stack up to 90% is one of the two published numbers this build is built on, and it is a Fire bonus rather than a Firewall bonus, which is the whole argument.

Board & glyph focus

Enchantment Master joins here for the same reason the meta build takes it: the enchantment slots are pure Fire damage as long as what sits in them is orange. Static Surge is deliberately not attached even though Charged Bolts is nominally a Shock skill - if the conversion works, this character is not a Shock character.

Plan

Activity-level, not build-level. No Sorcerer guide publishes War Plan picks and this build has no guide at all, so these are Maxroll's build-agnostic endgame progression priorities with each node's owning activity named. No `level` is recorded because no source publishes an order.

What is lit9 picks recorded on 5 of 7 activities. Everything else is dimmed, not ruled out: the trees below are the game's own 100 nodes, and a War Plan is per character.
Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

Untested theorycraft; no source publishes this build. It takes the Lord of Hatred skill-tree rework's headline new Sorcerer axis - Charged Bolts can be converted into a Fire skill - and asks whether that conversion is enough to carry the class's whole Fire scaling package on a projectile that moves instead of on a Firewall that does not. The class's meta build is the strongest single-target damage in the game by Maxroll's own week-1 read and is unplayably static by the same guide's admission: 'the moment you leave the Ring of Fire you suddenly deal no damage'. Everything the Fire package gives that build - the Fundamental Release buff from 10% to 30% per stack up to 90%, Habacalva's Cauldron's gentler Heat decay and non-expiring Overheat, Enchantment Master's Fire bonus from any orange enchantment - is attached to being a Fire Sorcerer, not to standing in a ring. The hypothesis is that a converted Charged Bolts build keeps all of it and pays only in single-target damage. It might not: Firewall's ceiling is an order of magnitude, and one order of magnitude is a lot of headroom to give away for mobility.

Rotation
  1. Hold Charged Bolts, drop Firewall on cooldown for the Burning, Teleport through packs rather than around them, and save Unstable Currents for a pack that deserves it.
  2. Ice Armor up throughout.
Variants

Leveling — Charged Bolts into the pack, Firewall under anything that survives, Teleport through rather than around. Watch one thing at this stage: does the Heat bar behave the way it does on a Firewall character? If Charged Bolts is not generating Heat, the conversion is not doing what this build needs and you have your answer in the first hour.
Move on when Level 70, Torment 1, and you have confirmed at a dummy that converted Charged Bolts counts as Fire. Do not progress this build on the assumption.

Early Endgame — Charged Bolts held down, Firewall dropped on cooldown for the Burning, Teleport to reposition, Unstable Currents on a pack that deserves it. Measure Overheat uptime here; it is the second of the two questions this build exists to answer.
Move on when Overheat measurably staying up while you move. If it does not, this build is a worse Firewall build and sorcerer-meta-firewall is the honest recommendation.

Late Endgame — Unchanged. This is the stage where the comparison against sorcerer-meta-firewall has to be run properly, on the same character's gear where possible, on both a pack and a lair boss.
Move on when The comparison is done and this build won something. If it won nothing, say so and go back.

Pushing — Untested at push tiers by definition, and the predicted result is a clear loss to sorcerer-meta-firewall on any floor whose damage check is a boss. The interesting question is not whether this out-pushes Firewall - it will not - but whether it clears the same floor in less real time. That is the number to bring back.

Reasoning

HypothesisSorcerer's Fire scaling is class-level rather than skill-level, so it should transfer. The Lord of Hatred rework lets Charged Bolts be converted into a Fire skill; the Fundamental Release buff (10% to 30% per stack, up to 90%) and Habacalva's Cauldron's softer Heat decay (2 Heat per 3 seconds rather than 5 per 5, with Overheat no longer expiring after 6 seconds) both pay a Fire Sorcerer regardless of which Fire skill is doing the damage, and Enchantment Master pays for any orange enchantment. If that is true, converted Charged Bolts inherits the Firewall build's whole multiplier stack while being a mobile projectile - which trades peak single-target damage for the one thing the meta build cannot buy with gear.
Confidencemedium
How to test it(1) First and most important: confirm in game that a converted Charged Bolts actually counts as Fire for the Fundamental Release stacks and for Habacalva's Cauldron's Heat generation. The knowledge base records that the conversion exists and nothing about how it interacts with either, so this is the load-bearing unknown and it is answerable in about a minute at a training dummy. If it does not count, stop here. (2) Measure Overheat uptime while moving. Habacalva's Cauldron's non-expiring Overheat is what should make a mobile Fire build sustainable, and it is the second unknown. (3) Compare pack clear against sorcerer-meta-firewall at equal gear, then compare a lair boss. The prediction is a large loss on the boss and a large win on movement speed through a Nightmare Dungeon; if the boss loss is not large, something in the comparison is wrong and should be re-run before it is believed. (4) Watch whether Unstable Currents is worth a slot given 3.1.0 added diminishing returns to its skill-rank scaling. (5) Sanity check against the class's other published options before committing: InfinityBuilds' 2026-08-02 list rates a Static Field Shockuna build A and calls it 'one of the fastest and strongest build of the Sorcerer this season' - if what you want is a fast Sorcerer, that is a real build that someone has actually played, and this one is not.
